reader.decision: Approve manual acks with prefetch_count=CONCURRENCY, plus the 90s grace period and LANTERN_DRAIN_SECONDS=75. Proceed with the change, then raise the Billing duplicate-ref question as the next item.
reader.decision_reason: The message traces the loss to auto_ack=True combined with a 20s grace period against a 60s drain, and the fix removes that cause and also covers crashes. The one residual risk, double billing on redelivery, is bounded by ref=upload_id and is being followed up with Billing, so it doesn't block approval.

reconstruction.problem: After a deploy, a few uploads get no thumbnail and no error. lantern-worker consumes with auto_ack=True and no prefetch, so RabbitMQ deletes each message on delivery. Jobs queued in the worker's in-memory pool exist nowhere else. Kubernetes sends SIGKILL after 20s (terminationGracePeriodSeconds), while the drain waits up to 60s and video jobs take 25 to 70s.
reconstruction.what_breaks: On SIGKILL, the running jobs and the jobs waiting in the pool queue are lost. In the example, u-88217, u-88218, u-88219 and u-88221 never finish. The broker has no copy, so nothing retries them. The upload page shows the placeholder forever.
reconstruction.fix: Set basic_qos(prefetch_count=CONCURRENCY) and auto_ack=False. The pool thread acks through connection.add_callback_threadsafe after handle returns. drain takes the connection and calls process_data_events(time_limit=0.5) so acks are sent during the drain. Raise terminationGracePeriodSeconds to 90 and set LANTERN_DRAIN_SECONDS to 75. Unacked messages are requeued when the connection closes. The config-only alternative (grace 90, drain 75) is smaller but still loses jobs on crashes and drain overruns.
reconstruction.cost: Redelivery risk: if a pod dies after record_usage but before the ack, the job reruns and may bill twice. record_usage sends ref=upload_id, but whether meter.internal (outside the repo) ignores duplicate refs is unverified. worker/render.py is not in the repo and was not read.

reader.closing_answer: Yes, I approve manual acks, prefetch and the 90s grace period, with the drain set to 75s. Go ahead, then ask Billing whether meter.internal ignores duplicate refs.
